summary: Preparing a shown V as a chain of requests, each with its reason, its fallbacks and its owner for every failure, from the view to the decoded resources and back to her parts on screen.

steps.does: A visible view shows a scene; the scene asks for the V it shows, for the reason that it is shown.
Keyed by the V: a newer request for the same V replaces the older; asking again within 30 s joins the work already there.
Asks the host for the V's character request, naming this page as the requester.
Shared by every page asking for the same character request; superseded only by the same page's newer request for the same V.
Answers from a kept record, or prepares it, asking for each resource it needs.
One export per resource, shared by every preparation that needs it.
Ranked approaches: the native decoder first, WolvenKit next.
Runs within a 10 s budget that pauses while it is suspended; over budget or unsupported, the request moves to WolvenKit with the time it has left.
The second approach; with no usable WolvenKit it suspends and asks for it to be set up.
Raised to fix the suspended work, for the reason that the person consented to exactly this release; answering it resumes everything waiting.
The page loads the record into the V's runtime in that scene.
One per V and scene, made on first demand and collected 2 s after no view shows her.
One per part content; a part lingers 30 s after its last use, so flicking back or clicking a hovered choice is free.
Swaps the new parts in at once and releases the old ones to linger.

demand: The visible view: view → scene → V → preparation → exports → decodes; nothing is prepared for a V no visible view shows, except what lingers.

faults.when: The page sends a character request the host doesn't accept.
A native decode runs past its budget.
The native reader doesn't read this kind of resource.
No usable WolvenKit; the preparation waits, and the person sees one next step.
The person's consent was for another release, or was withdrawn; the setup ends and asks again.
The masculine core can't be prepared; the feminine core stands in, with a notice.
Every approach failed; the V stays as shown, with Try again, which retries from the first approach.

latency: Prepared and lingering: shown again in under 200 ms, with no work redone.
Kept record on the host: shown in under 1 s.
Cold preparation: progress shown in place at once; no decode waits more than 10 s before WolvenKit takes over.
budget.memory: Parts linger 30 s and V runtimes 2 s after their last use; nothing else is kept for a V no view shows.

invariants: Every running piece of work traces to a visible view through a chain of requests, each with a reason.
A page's newer request for a V ends only that page's older request for the same V.
Every failure has one holder: the page for its own bad input, the next approach for a failed one, then the person.
Work waiting for WolvenKit is paused, not torn down, and carries on once it is set up.
A view never shows a V's parts from two different records at once.
